newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended just lower on Thursday, taking a breather after two days of hectic gains in which the AEX index climbed nearly six percent, with investors wary and looking to take some profits, dealers said.
The index was supported throughout the session by a storming performance from Philips Electronics shares, sparked by better-than-expected second quarter results.

Philips, Europe's biggest consumer electronics group, reported net profit from ordinary operations more than doubled to 693 million guilders, from 304 million in the same period of 1996. The rise was well above analysts' estimates.
Its shares smashed through their prior year high at the open, gaining over eight percent as investors registered their approval.
Philips ended up 9.20 guilders, 5.68 percent, at 171.30 compared to a prior year-high of 165.30. The shares traded as high as 177.00 guilders on the day.
Six analysts spoken to by Reuters said a share price target of 200 guilders by the end of the year seemed realistic if the stock continued its current bullish trend.
"To begin with, the stock will get a big boost from all the e.p.s. upgrades we're going to see," one said.

The AEX started weak, with only Philips bucking the overall trend to take profits after two days of big gains, but began to rally in the late afternoon as the dollar flirted with six-year highs in Europe before slipping with Wall Street at the close.
Dealers said a respite from macroeconomic worries was allowing the market to again focus on individual stocks, with several issues in focus.

Software company Baan saw its second quarter results less well received than Philips', though its net income compared to the same period last year more than doubled to $16.4 million, in the middle of analysts' forecast range.
Baan shares were the biggest loser on the AMX midcap index, shedding 16.80 guilders, over ten percent, to 146.70.

A trader said much of the selling pressure in the stock was out of the U.S., where Baan was downgraded by both Smith Barney, to neutral from outperform, and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, to accumulate from buy.

CD maker DOCdata was strong as the market digested results and forecasts presented on Wednesday and some encouraging broker reports, traders said. DOCdata said on Wednesday it saw good growth and a big acquisition in prospect this year.
The shares rose 1.50 guilders, 5.51 percent, to a new year-high of 28.70 guilders.

TV producer Endemol, under the cosh in recent months, also performed well after announcing an acquisition in Spain. Endemol said it had bought a 45 percent stake in Spanish production company Zeppelin and had the option to acquire a "substantial majority" of Zeppelin shares in the future.
Its shares added 2.20 guilders, 4.57 percent, to 50.30.
Food group BolsWessanen rose to a year high, gaining 2.40 guilders, 5.73 percent, to 44.30.
Dealers cited long-standing market talk of merger activity, which has assumed new prominence recently and stimulated high trading volumes in the stock.
Blue chips and financial stocks were weak on Thursday, reflecting their prominence in the big rises of the last two days, dealers said.
